title: Structured logging — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, an incident reviewer asks what a log event contains. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences on the fields a log event carries, one field excluded on purpose, and why the exclusion matters.

vocabulary.meaning: recording enough to diagnose an incident while carrying nothing that would harm if the log were read by anyone
a value deliberately kept out of a log line, named in the design so that it is not reintroduced later

expectedElements: The event fields are enumerated concretely
One deliberately excluded field is named
The diagnostic value of the remaining fields is defended
modelAnswer: Each log event carries a timestamp, a correlation identifier, the operation name, the outcome, the duration, and the identifier of the affected record. The request body is deliberately excluded, and that exclusion is written into the design so it is not reintroduced as an oversight. The reason is that a log is read by more people than the database, and the body contains customer data. The remaining fields still provide enough evidence to reconstruct an incident through the correlation and record identifiers.
commonMistakes: Describing logging as safe without naming a single excluded field
Excluding fields so aggressively that no incident can be reconstructed
variants: Rewrite the update as the logging rule for a new service.
